title: Small good subsets with a controlled intersection
statement: Use the universe, regularity, presentability, weak saturation and tree definitions in [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation]. Fix infinite regular cardinals $\kappa<\tau$, with $\tau$ uncountable and $a^b<\tau$ for all cardinals $a<\tau$ and $b<\kappa$. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary locally $\tau$-presentable category with small Hom sets. Let $C,W$ be arrow classes, with $C$ and $C\cap W$ weakly saturated. Suppose $W$ is closed under isomorphism of arrows, has two-out-of-three for composable arrows, and has the following approximation property: for every small $\tau$-filtered poset $P$, every diagram $p\mapsto f_p$ of arrows with $\tau$-presentable sources and targets whose colimit in the arrow category lies in $W$, and every subset $E\subseteq P$ of size less than $\tau$, there is a subset $Q\subseteq P$ containing $E$, with $|Q|<\tau$, which is $\kappa$-filtered in its inherited order and whose arrow colimit belongs to $W$. Here two-out-of-three means that membership of two of $f,g,gf$ implies membership of the third. Let $L\subseteq C$ have $\tau$-presentable sources and targets and let a $\tau$-good $L$-tree with root $X$ be given, indexed by $T$, with $X\to Y_T$ in $W$. Call a subset $B\subseteq T$ good when it is downward-closed and $X\to Y_B$ belongs to $W$. For every good $A_0\subseteq T$ and every subset $B_0\subseteq T$ of size less than $\tau$, there exists a good $B\subseteq T$ with $|B|<\tau$ containing $B_0$, such that $B\cap A_0$ is good as well.

source.place: Proof of Lemma A.2.6.9, observation (ii) and claim (*) with its alternating enlargement construction (printed pp. 822-823). The hypothesis that the whole tree is good is explicit here. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this cellular-tree result.

proof.text: First establish the increasing-union rule for good subsets. If $D\subseteq E$ are good, the relative-tree clause of [lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation], together with $L\subseteq C$ and weak saturation of $C$, puts $Y_D\to Y_E$ in $C$. Both maps from $X$ are in $W$, so two-out-of-three puts this transition in $W$. For an increasing ordinal-indexed family $(D_i)$ of good subsets, set $D_{<j}=\bigcup_{i<j}D_i$ at limit stages. Colimits of these restricted trees have the union property: a cocone under $X$ over the union is exactly a compatible cocone over each restriction, since every cell and every order relation is already in some restriction. Thus $Y_{D_{<j}}$ is the colimit of the earlier $Y_{D_i}$. Transfinite induction now shows that each $D_{<j}$ is good: at a successor use two-out-of-three as above, and at a limit the continuous composite from $X$ has all its transitions in $C\cap W$, so weak saturation puts that composite in $C\cap W$. The empty case starts at $Y_\varnothing=X$ and $1_X\in C\cap W$. Consequently every increasing union of good subsets is good. We will only need countable unions.

source.place: A.2.6.9, observation (i), p. 822; elementary expansion of continuity using cocones.

proof.text: We next prove a small-good-enlargement rule inside an arbitrary good downward-closed $G\subseteq T$. Fix $E\subseteq G$ with $|E|<\tau$. Restriction to $G$ is still a $\tau$-good $L$-tree with root $X$. Apply [lem-coef-cellular-tree-presentable-approximations] to this restricted tree. It supplies a small $\tau$-filtered poset $P$ and arrows $h_p$ with $\tau$-presentable endpoints whose arrow colimit is $X\to Y_G$. Choose $p_0$ whose support contains $E$. This arrow colimit is in $W$ because $G$ is good, so the approximation property assumed in the statement, with prescribed subset $\{p_0\}\subseteq P$, gives a $\kappa$-filtered $Q\subseteq P$ with $p_0\in Q$, $|Q|<\tau$ and $h_Q=\operatorname{colim}_{q\in Q}h_q\in W$. This is an application of the stated approximation hypothesis, not of closure of $W$ under filtered colimits.

source.place: A.2.6.9, observation (ii), p. 822: make explicit the presentable-endpoint diagram to which the approximation property applies.

proof.text: Set $D=S_Q=\bigcup_{q\in Q}S_q$. It is downward-closed in $G$, hence in $T$, and contains $E$ through $S_{p_0}$. Regularity of $\tau$ gives $|D|<\tau$, since $|Q|<\tau$ and each support has size less than $\tau$. As $\kappa$ is infinite, the $\kappa$-filtered poset $Q$ is nonempty and filtered. The final clause of [lem-coef-cellular-tree-presentable-approximations] therefore applies: $h_Q$ lies in the weakly saturated closure of $L$, hence in $C$, and its pushout along $M_Q\to X$ is $X\to Y_D$. Step 2 gives $h_Q\in W$, so $h_Q\in C\cap W$. Weak saturation of $C\cap W$ puts its pushout $X\to Y_D$ in $W$. Thus $D$ is a small good subset with $E\subseteq D\subseteq G$. In particular this argument never infers that a filtered colimit of arbitrary $C$-arrows lies in $C$; the cited node gives an actual cellular tree for $h_Q$.

source.place: A.2.6.9, observation (ii), p. 822: agent expansion for a possibly non-presentable root; push out an arrow of C intersect W.

proof.text: Define sequences $B_n\subseteq T$ and $D_n\subseteq A_0$, initially $B_0$ as in the statement and $D_0=A_0\cap B_0$. Assuming $B_n,D_n$ have cardinality less than $\tau$, use the small-good-enlargement rule of Steps 2-3 inside the good set $T$ on $B_n\cup D_n$ to choose a good $B_{n+1}$ containing that union and of size less than $\tau$. The set $T$ is good by the whole-tree hypothesis. Use the rule a second time, inside the good set $A_0$, on $A_0\cap B_{n+1}$ to choose a good $D_{n+1}\subseteq A_0$ containing that intersection and of size less than $\tau$. This defines both sequences for every natural number. They are increasing: $B_n\subseteq B_{n+1}$, and $D_n\subseteq A_0\cap B_{n+1}\subseteq D_{n+1}$. Also $D_n\subseteq B_{n+1}$ for every $n$. Only the tails starting at index 1 are asserted to be good and downward-closed.

source.place: A.2.6.9, claim (*) and its alternating construction, pp. 822-823; recursion using the rule already proved in Steps 2-3.

proof.text: Put $B=\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n$. Its good tail $B_1\subseteq B_2\subseteq\cdots$ has the same union, so Step 1 proves $B$ good. The same rule proves $D=\bigcup_{n<\omega}D_n$ good. The inclusions of Step 4 identify $D=A_0\cap B$: each $D_n$ lies in $A_0\cap B_{n+1}$, while each $A_0\cap B_n$ lies in $D_n$ for $n\geq1$ (and this holds at $n=0$ by definition). Since $\tau$ is uncountable regular, this countable union of sets of size less than $\tau$ has size less than $\tau$. It contains the original $B_0$. Therefore $B$ and $B\cap A_0$ satisfy all the required conclusions.

source.place: A.2.6.9, end of the proof of claim (*), p. 823; equality of unions and the uncountable regular size bound.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-e3e95a65f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item's statement is byte-identical to the live side DAG (still unsplit there), so nothing was weakened. Step 1 (good subsets are closed under increasing unions): this follows from the relative-tree clause of lem-coef-weak-saturation-tree-presentation (with L in C and C weakly saturated), two-out-of-three, the cocone union property from def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, and continuous transfinite composition in C∩W; the empty case is 1_X. Steps 2-3: applied to the downward-closed G, the new node gives τ-filtered h_p with τ-presentable endpoints and colimit X→Y_G in W. The item's own approximation hypothesis with {p_0} then gives a κ-filtered Q with h_Q in W. The filtered-restriction clause (κ infinite, so Q is nonempty and filtered) gives h_Q in the closure of L, hence in C, with pushout X→Y_{S_Q}. Pushout closure of C∩W makes S_Q good, and regularity gives |S_Q|<τ. No filtered-colimit closure of C or W is assumed, and X is never assumed presentable. Steps 4-5 follow the alternating B_n/D_n recursion. I checked D_n ⊆ A_0∩B_{n+1} ⊆ D_{n+1}, the equality ∪D_n = A_0∩∪B_n including n=0, and the countable size bound. The parent's Step 6 uses the item correctly (κ:=λ). New node lem-coef-cellular-tree-presentable-approximations: statement-only, self-contained, three kinds of Mathlib search, blueprint from/via correct. I tested it on T empty, one cell, chains (downward closure of a set of size <τ stays <τ) and presentability of N_p. The filtered-restriction clause holds because the colimit over the cofinal upward-closed set of q with t in S_q keeps P_t and Q_t fixed, and colimits of pushouts are pushouts. It is not a duplicate of small-cellular-tree-descent (which needs |T|<τ), weak-saturation-tree-presentation, accessible-subdiagram-criterion or the Smith nodes, and it does not restate a clause of the item (it has no W). All dependencies are in the same unit or are the colimit definition, so there are no tool_uses and no cycle. No fixes were needed. HTT is not archived and network access is blocked, so I could not read A.2.6.9 or A.1.5.11 myself. Both nodes are marked as agent proofs and the WANTED line stands; I checked the mathematics independently in full.
